reviews.text: I found this game on Steam a few weeks ago while idly searching for Western games. Whether or not it actually qualifies in this category, I'm not really sure, but I decided to buy it for its name anyway to see what it's about. The funny thing about video games is that nothing about them matters except whether or not they're fun to play. After loading Cowboy 3030 up, I didn't think I would like it. It's fairly low fidelity, has no public multiplayer (at least yet), and feels sort of like a game you might have found on XBLA c. 2010. The currently available options are particularly bad right now--I was having nasty screen tearing even with my framerate capped, and there was no vsync--but may be expanded in EA. Who knows. But I played a few runs anyway. And as I got into it, I realized that I actually was having a lot of fun. As a 3D movement shooter, Cowboy 3030 is pretty good. Enemy attacks are telegraphed in fair but challenging ways. The guns feel relatively powerful. Movement is precise. The skill trees made me roll my eyes at first, but once you get a handle on them, they're actually full of extremely powerful upgrades that can totally change the way you play, and they're enough to make the runs feel different. The environments are samey. And it's hard not to feel like you're in 3D Ultra Minigolf Adventures when you're progressing down a linear canyon of near-identical, vaguely Western environments. But it's serviceable. If you're willing to take a chance on Early Access, and especially if you have a feel friends who feel similarly, Cowboy 3030 is worth trying. There aren't that many 3D games that do bullet hell as well as this one.
Give this a shot if you like: - Risk of Rain 2 - Bullet Hell - Cowboys - Cacti Honestly, it's quite nice for it's value and will receive a ton of updates yet. Multiplayer is smooth as well.

GAWD DAMN! I'm fightin for my life but the hardest opponent has to be the riddle bot. What ya mean I failed at this riddle? Yeah well screw ya I think I'm right and BzzZzzt! Near dead! Would be nice if theres a Yes or No option to the riddle bot though. Other than that, what in tarnation is this game? Well sit down and listen to ye ole pawpaw, this old man gotta ask if you know what is a rogue-like game. Its a game where your previous save doesn't affect your future game right? Well damn siree you're right! Not only is this game a rogue-like game, even the talent tree is not constant, it changes with every game you play, forcing you to strategise which is the fun part! There is no meta-build when nothing is constant! There are so far there characters as of 30 May 2024, Keli, Calix and Teri. Keli is a long-range sniper specialist. Sometimes she get other rifle-type weapons as well. Calix is your ole beloved traditional cowboy with a pistol! Teri meanwhile is a shotgun specialist. All he gets is shotgun type weapons! So far everything feels balanced and its fun to shoot em damn robots. I expect there will be more fun updates in the future with more variety of characters and weapons. Get this game if you're into FPS, rogue-like games! You won't be disappointed with the price its offering now. Anyway, that is all and thanks for listenin to ye ole pawpaw.

This game is a ton of fun. I highly recommend it for people looking for unique combat. If you care a ton about animations and polish, some of the animations can be jerky, but if you care about interesting gameplay and progression then this game is great. The random progression tree is very interesting, it can be a game in itself. It was intimidating the first time I saw it but after I understood it I realized it has alot of depth and feels very rewarding. It rewards you for planning ahead and synergizing. I highly recommend this game especially if you have friends for co op.

The more I play, the more I'm impressed by the balance this game strikes. On the one hand, it's comfortably familiar to us Action Roguelike fans, with addicting gameplay cycles and different play styles for each character. On the other hand, it's also very unique, and introduces a lot of new elements and ideas to the genre. Everything from the upgrade system down to the combat itself have their own distinct flavors. I think the developer is putting a lot of effort into making this more than just another roguelike. If you're familiar with the Action Roguelike genre, I absolutely think this is worth a try (the demo gives a good idea of what to expect from the full game). I suspect I still have a few dozen hours left to 100% everything, and I look forward to it.

It plays INCREDIBLY good, seriously. The shooting feels pretty well with all weapons, each with their own way to handle and gimmicks. The movement is sharp and responsive, with good hitboxes for the attacks and few but nice options to dodge (which can be upgraded too). The other thing that this game excels at is the originality and variety of mechanics of the characters and weapons, having to adapt yourself to each occasion, simple things like being able to see the spread of shotguns or a different way to reload faster make the gameplay feel unique and interesting. The designs of the maps and the cowboys does seem... bland and uninteresting, but the enemies and especially bosses make up for that, with frenetic fights and attacks. I do wish there was more spacial sounds for when the enemies appear each zone though (there's only visual indication), and obviously more distinct maps, as they only change visually the more one progress. I'm surprised how good it plays, it's very fun and addictive, with a lot of bosses and guns to try. I really recommend it. Esp: Se juega INCREÍBLEMENTE bien, en serio. El shooting se siente bastante bien con todas las armas, cada una con su propia forma de manejarse y truquitos. El movimiento es rapido y responsivo, con buenas hitboxes para los ataques y pocas pero buenas opciones para esquivar (que también se pueden mejorar). La otra cosa en la que destaca es en la originalidad y variedad de mecánicas de los personajes y las armas, teniendo que adaptarte a cada ocasión, cosas simples como poder ver la dispersión de las escopetas o una forma diferente de recargar más rápido hacen que la jugabilidad se sienta única e interesante. Los diseños de los mapas y los vaqueros sí son... sosos y poco interesantes, pero los enemigos y sobre todo los jefes lo compensan, con combates y ataques frenéticos. Eso sí, me gustaría que se pudiesen distinguir mejor donde aparecen los enemigos en cada zona con el audio (solo te lo indica visualmente), y obviamente mapas más diferenciados, ya que sólo cambian visualmente cuanto más se avanza. Me sorprendió lo bien que se juega, es muy divertido y adictivo, con un montón de jefes y armas que probar. La verdad que lo recomiendo bastante.

Not recommended at this time. While it has potential it is very repetitive, the "hallway"-sections are tedious as hell. Most characters have 1 single skill that breaks them completely. This just shows the lack of testing and lack of thought that go into this game. Similarly, who the hell thought adding a mandatory shoot all the barrels for 1 coin and walk around collecting it mod was a good idea?? It's OP as ♥♥♥♥ and at the same time super tedious.

[h1]Cowboy 3030, a visually weak looking 3rd person shooter roguelike, a gameplay strong feeling 3rd person shooter roguelike[/h1] Cowboy 3030 is a roguelike where you basically enter a wild-west looking "street", X amount of enemies appear and it's up to you finish them off before they finish you. As someone whom have played way too many roguelikes and roguelites, on paper Cowboy 3030 is something that should drop my interest very soon and be slammed with red colored thumb down review. The streets are very same looking after first time you enter one and at the very end of a run, the roguelike upgrades you gather during a run are quite unimaginative and mostly just "shield +X amount" or "firerate +X amount", chapter bosses are always the same (new boss designs are saved to NG+ runs) and guns you collect during a run are not too different from each other (each weapon category is saved for spesific classes, like only one gets sniper, while other only gets light machine guns etc.). However, where Cowboy 3030 very strongly shines is in it's gameplay, something that looking through gameplay videos doesn't easily come up but as you get to play it yourself you can feel you have a good time. Player character controls work well and enemy attack patterns are challenging yet avoidable when you focus to combat. In other words when you must focus to avoiding enemy attacks, that's when Cowboy 3030 is "the good s###". [h2]Verdict:[/h2] While Cowboy 3030 looks very simplistic in it's visuals and fails to follow good roguelike recepies (varying boss challenges in end of chapter [until you beat the game once] and upgrades are 90% boring stuff), it shines in it's gameplay. Despite the strong gameplay, I woudn't recommend this game at it's full price with current amount of content but it's a good pick on sale. And if nothing else, this would be a very strong job-application if people whom worked on this game were to apply work in bigger game studios that are spesialized in 3rd person "bullet hells" like Housemarque, Platinum games or Gearbox.

Played once in '24 (EA) and once in '25 (1.0). In '24 I was left with the feeling of "this is fun, just needs fleshing out". After playing it again in '25 I'm left with the feeling of "why did I waste my cash on this random crap?" Played through it once both times (approx 20 mins). Like others say, it feels like a PS2 game through and through. As soon as you've played the first "rotation" you've played them all.

Competent bullet-hell shooter but lacks in comparison to games like ROR2 and Gun fire reborn. The levels are fun, a bit samey and not quite enough interesting stuff going on, but they do the job. The enemies are the stand out, interesting bullet hell mechanics and fire patterns, feels tricky but fair. Movement is fine, the characters are responsive, they could use a little more visual feedback and the dodge through bullets is a cool mechanic. Where the game really falls flat is the advancement. The game is far too balanced, every run feels very 'samey' because there are only a few improvements to get per character and there is fairly minimal stacking. They even have a cool grid boosting that could be perfect for stacking but they don't let you do it so it just ends up being extremely constrained. This just makes every run feel pretty much like the last run. It makes for a game that's fun for a few hours but quickly loses it's shine. I'd say it's a good grab for under 5 dollars but probably not worth full price even at 15 dollars. The game also lacks tons of QOL features, no run stats, character details etc. It's kind of maddening because they clearly track this stuff they just choose not to display it. It's a shame the game has fine old school bones but it feels too much like the devs weren't willing to let it 'find the fun' and failed to add in that final polish.
